title: Cardinal Burke initiates 5-year spiritual journey for Guadalupe’s 500th anniversary
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — Cardinal Raymond Burke, one of the most influential figures in the American hierarchy and a longtime proponent of traditional Catholic devotion, has invited the faithful to join him in a five-year spiritual journey of Marian formation leading to the 500th anniversary of the apparitions of Our Lady of Guadalupe. In a message shared on X, the cardinal from Wisconsin announced “ Semper Virgo ,” a daily email program of contemplations that will begin on December 12 — the feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe — and continue until the quincentennial on December 12, 2031. … The cardinal’s invitation comes as other initiatives prepare for the same anniversary. Archbishop Salvatore Cordileone of San Francisco has launched “Project Guadalupe 2031,” encouraging family consecrations and home enthronements of her image in response to a call for a nine-year novena. Burke’s own previous nine-month novena to Our Lady of Guadalupe drew nearly 190,000 registered participants worldwide. Registration for the free daily emails is available at the Semper Virgo website included in the cardinal’s message. “It is my fervent prayer that these five years of preparation will be a time of true conversion of heart, of renewed devotion to the Blessed Virgin Mary, and of ever closer union with her Divine Son, so that we may worthily celebrate this jubilee,” Burke concluded. “May the Ever-Perfect Virgin Mary, Our Lady of Guadalupe, Mother of God and Mother of the Church, lead us ever more faithfully to her Divine Son, Our Lord Jesus Christ, Who alone is our salvation.”

title: New study shows just 29% of Catholics believe in Real Presence in Eucharist
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — A recently published study that surveyed over 1,000 Catholics found only about 29%, less than a third, believe in the Church’s central dogma : Our Lord Jesus Christ is truly present in the Holy Eucharist, just years after U.S. bishops began a Eucharistic revival initiative. The alarming study , published in the academic journal Sociological Inquiry in September, shows that just 28.8% of the 1,049 faithful surveyed answered that they believe that “the bread and wine truly become the Body and Blood of Christ” during the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass. About 58.8% of self-identified Catholics said the bread and wine “are just symbols,” and approximately 12.4% said they were “not sure what happens.” … However, the U.S. bishops largely declined to even discuss the survey results with the RPC. “One would think that the ‘listening Church’ would be bending over backwards to ‘listen’ to the voices of thousands of lay Catholics on why they felt there had been a loss of faith in the Real Presence and their recommendations on how this problem could best be addressed,” a member of the Coalition, who preferred to remain anonymous, previously told LifeSite. “One would think that the leaders of the Eucharistic Revival would be beating down the doors of the RPC to understand the thoughts of those who had been surveyed,” they added. “But, alas, this was not the case. (In) fact, it seemed the bishops went out of their way to avoid hearing about the survey results.”
